the D1 receptor is involved in working memory and that the D1 and D2 receptors are involved in the modulation of the excitability of pyramidal cells in the cortex.

D1 receptors in prefrontal cortex are critical for cognitive processes such as short term memory, attentional control of sensory processing, and the ability of prefrontal neurons to integrate information from multiple sources.

the DA innervation in the prefronton cortex is involved in a number of cognitive processes, including attention, working memory, reward and reinforcement, and the integration of high level sensory inputs, and that these functions are mediated via specific DA receptors and receptor subtypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DA innervation in the prefrontals is organized to modulate the ability of cortical circuits to process information in working memory, and that this modulation is mediated by D1* receptors.

the prefrontal DA innervation is organized to modulate the activity and connectivity of pyramidal neurons in the prefrontial cortex, and that this modulatory influence is mediated via specific DA receptors and their subcellular distribution in prefrontal circuits.

D1* receptors are involved in the maintenance of information in working memory and in cognitive flexibility, and D2* receptors are involved with the initiation of cognitive activity and with cognitive inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DA receptors are a family of receptors that have distinct anatomical and physiological functions.

the D1 receptor is the major target for the action of DA in modulating the excitatory drive on pyramidal cells and the D2 receptor is primarily involved in regulating the inhibitory input on these same cells.
the DA receptors that are most likely to mediate DA's actions in prefrontal cortex are those that are expressed on the dendrites of cortical pyramidal neurons.
